sentences.text: Final pharmacy release occurs only after the order, prepared medication, and intended destination have been checked against the approved dispensing instructions.
The Clinical Pharmacist reviews clinical and labeling exceptions that require professional judgment before authorizing release.
The Pharmacy Technician confirms that the package contents and patient identifiers match the verified order.
The Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot presents the completed package at the Pharmacy Verification Station for the final check.
The Pharmacy Verification Station records the verification outcome and prevents release while required checks remain incomplete.
The Pharmacy Verification Station produces the Batch Release Note after the final release checks are recorded.
The release decision is associated with the order identifier, package identifier, verification time, and responsible staff credentials.
The Medication Order Gateway provides the current order status used to confirm that the request remains valid.
A canceled, duplicated, or superseded request is held for resolution rather than placed into a delivery load.
The Clinical Pharmacist documents the disposition of any clinical concern before the package can proceed.
Supporting records are prepared before a load enters the delivery network so staff can establish what was released and under which conditions.
The load manifest identifies each package, its intended destination, handling requirements, and the time it was assembled.
Package identifiers are checked against the manifest to detect omissions, substitutions, or duplicate entries.
Temperature-sensitive packages remain under controlled conditions until their custody is formally transferred.
The Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler records temperature conditions while medication awaits transfer.
At the physical handoff, the Hospital Courier checks package count, packaging integrity, destination information, and any special handling instructions.
The courier records the time and identity associated with acceptance so the custody history remains traceable.
The Hospital Courier produces the Pneumatic Capsule Seal Record when the capsule is sealed for transfer.
The courier verifies that the capsule is closed securely and that its contents are not exposed during handling.
The Pneumatic Tube Network accepts only loads that meet the applicable packaging and routing requirements.
The East Tube Dispatch Console checks the requested route and reports whether the route is available for dispatch.
Before a capsule is admitted, its package identifiers and destination are reconciled with the prepared load information.
A route or packaging problem places the load on hold until staff resolve the condition and document the outcome.
If automated transfer is unavailable, staff retain custody and use an approved alternate delivery procedure.
The receiving department confirms arrival and reports any discrepancy through the established operational process.
